## Triton expressiveness boundary
- Triton has no grid-level sync between programs — multi-CTA persistent
  kernels with cross-block dependencies need CUDA C++ (cooperative groups
  or counter protocols). Single-program kernels need no grid sync and ARE
  Triton-expressible.

falsifier: If the measured paired speedup lands at or below 1.03, the calibrated promotion threshold for shape 1, then host launch overhead was not a material share of this shape runtime and the graph-replay mechanism is not the shape-1 lever.
hypothesis: Replaying the entire shape-1 forward as one captured CUDA graph removes the per-call host launch cost that the baseline pays 115 times per forward, and on a shape whose achieved throughput is limited by latency rather than bandwidth that removal should show up as wall-clock win.
reasoning: The counter is measured on both routes with the same tool, not assumed: nsys on the un-graphed baseline reports 115 launch API calls per forward across 13 distinct kernels, and nsys plus torch-profiler independently agree the graphed route issues 2. roofline-table.md reads shape 1 as compute-bound at ideal fusion with achieved throughput at 36 percent of the fp16 roof, which is a latency and grid problem, so removing 113 host launches per forward attacks the actual limiter. On the band, stated plainly: the gate requires a relative width under 2 percent, so this is a committed point estimate and not the honest width of my uncertainty. The only idle-box evidence this project holds on comparable B-64 d-128 shapes reads 1.14x on shape 9 and 1.56x on shape 10, which bracket far wider than the permitted band, and both are pre-gate numbers that the post-LOCK re-measurement exists to replace. I take the lower anchor, 1.15, because shape 1 carries 4 heads against shape 9 with 1 and its roofline candidate time 0.6461 ms sits closest to shape 9 at 0.6113 ms. A result far above this band is therefore a band miss I expect to have to explain rather than a refutation of the mechanism.

# GEMM epilogue / elementwise fusion (researched 28-29 Aug 2026)

- cuBLAS 12.x fuses common epilogues (bias, GELU) with matmuls:
  https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/new-cublas-12-0-features-and-matrix-multiplication-performance-on-nvidia-hopper-gpus/
- Average ~1.45x for GEMMs with epilogue fusion where the elementwise tail
  was bandwidth-bound (survey via
  https://www.emergentmind.com/topics/fused-triton-kernels and tile-overlap
  paper https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02521v1).

falsifier: If k003 alone lands at or below 1.03, the calibrated shape-1 threshold, then the Triton attention is not the mechanism either and both the graph-replay and the fusion readings of attempt 1 are wrong.
hypothesis: The authored Triton flash attention, with no CUDA graph capture at all, is the mechanism that produced attempt 1 gain. It removes the repeated passes over the materialized 16.8 MB per-layer score tensor that the dense baseline route builds, so it should recover most of the measured speedup on its own.
reasoning: This band is derived from device-busy time on both routes rather than from any speedup row. nsys on the baseline reports 5.729 ms of GPU-busy per forward inside a 5.928 ms span, and torch-profiler on the graphed candidate reports 2.61 ms of GPU-busy per forward. Device work therefore roughly halves, and graph replay cannot cause that because it changes only how work is submitted. k003 runs the identical Triton kernel without capture, so it should do the same device work while still paying the baseline launch idle of about 0.199 ms per forward, giving 5.928 divided by 2.809, or about 2.11. Worth stating because it cuts against my own earlier conclusion: 2.10 predicted from device time is very close to the 2.0748 event speedup attempt 1 actually measured, while the wall speedup of 2.6043 is the arm that disagrees with everything. That suggests the event-timed number was closer to sound than I credited when I read the tripwire, and this screening run on a verified quiet box is the test that separates those readings.

summary: Screening cycle 3 closes the attribution loop. k003, the authored Triton attention with no graph capture, measured 1.6009665 paired against the shape-1 baseline on a verified deep-idle box in the scratch lane, correct on all seeds. The bound baseline profile caps what whole-forward graph replay can add on top at about 1.035x, because that route is GPU-busy 96.6 percent of its span with only 0.199 ms of launch idle per 5.928 ms forward. Those two numbers predict the bundled k004 at about 1.657x. Attempt 1 measured k004 at 2.0748x but on a contended box whose event-versus-wall tripwire fired at 1.2552 against a 1.0024 to 1.0391 calibration envelope, and 2.0748 divided by that ratio is 1.653, which is the same figure by a different and admittedly coincidental route. This cycle screens k004 on the quiet box to decide between the two readings directly instead of inferring.

summary: Shape-9 cycle, and a deliberate change of prediction method. Three bands tonight were derived from mechanism theory and all three missed: a launch-overhead ceiling of 1.035x that the measurement refuted at 1.338x, a device-time estimate of 2.10 for the un-graphed Triton arm that measured 1.6010, and a work-density scaling argument predicting shape 5 below shape 1 that measured 2.1475 against shape 1 2.1428. Two of those misses tripped falsifiers I had preregistered against my own position. The measured evidence says the bundled gain is invariant across a doubling of batch, which is the signature of a mechanism that scales with the work rather than with launch count. Shapes 1, 9, 10 and 11 are the same model differing only in head count with identical useful FLOPs, so shape 9 is predicted from the two nearest measured analogues at 2.12 to 2.16 rather than from any further theory.

## cuPilot — strategy-coordinated multi-agent kernel evolution

- cuBLAS 12.x fuses common epilogues (bias, GELU) with matmuls:
  https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/new-cublas-12-0-features-and-matrix-multiplication-performance-on-nvidia-hopper-gpus/

falsifier: If shape 13 lands at or above 4.5 then the fused kernel is not merely removing the elementwise and softmax traffic but also outperforming the baseline attention GEMMs substantially, which the 18.3 percent GEMM residual in my arithmetic assumes it does not.
hypothesis: At sequence length 1024 the baseline spends 71.2 percent of its device time on masked_fill, scale multiply and softmax over a materialized score tensor of about 1.07 GB per layer, and only 18.3 percent on the attention GEMMs themselves. A fused flash kernel deletes the traffic and keeps the GEMM work, so the residual should be roughly 28 percent of the original.
reasoning: Seven bands tonight, seven misses, every one of them set either by mechanism theory or by analogy to a different shape. This is the first band I have derived from a measured per-kernel time breakdown of the shape actually being predicted. The nsys baseline profile for shape 13 gives masked_fill 916269561 ns over 340 instances at 37.2 percent, the scale multiply 419627061 ns at 17.0 percent, softmax 417830332 ns at 17.0 percent, the two attention GEMMs at 9.2 and 9.1 percent, and the linear projection GEMMs at only 3.8 percent because attention is quadratic in sequence length while the projections are linear. Removing the 71.2 percent that is pure traffic over the score tensor while retaining the 18.3 percent GEMM share and the roughly 10 percent remainder leaves about 28 percent, hence 3.5x. I am recording in advance that if this band also misses, the honest conclusion is that I cannot forecast this system and should report characterization runs as measurements without numeric bands.
